summary: The note traces the history of rock climbing and bouldering from the 1920s to today, covering the evolution of gear from hemp ropes and pitons to clean-climbing protection and spring-loaded cams. It also describes how technique advanced with indoor gyms and technique clinics, how bouldering grew as a rope-free form, and how local climbers now mentor newcomers.
one_line: A historical overview of rock climbing and bouldering gear, technique, and culture, from 1920s pioneers to local climbers mentoring today's newcomers.
key_facts: In the 1920s climbers used hemp ropes, handforged metal spikes, heavy tweed and leather hobnail boots; George Mallory influenced the ethos of climbing as a pursuit in its own right.
John Salathé, a Yosemite legend who immigrated to America in 1939, shaped pitons out of discarded automobile parts that were stronger and more durable than European gear.
In the 1960s Royal Robbins and Yvon Chouinard advocated clean climbing, which sought to preserve rock faces and led to passive protection such as nuts and hexes that needed no hammering.
Ray Jardine innovated spring-loaded camming devices in 1978; these 'friends' revolutionized protection and became a staple of a climber's rack.
Alex Grant and Sarah Levin have pioneered numerous local routes since the late 2000s and say the climbing community has grown unprecedentedly since September of 2023.
Laybacking, jamming, and edging are fundamental techniques refined by past climbers that remain valuable today.

Jeff Johnson, who has been scaling walls since the '80s, attests to changes in climbing styles; indoor gyms introduced in the 1990s let climbers train consistently and develop more gymnastic, dynamic movements.
Technique clinics, once an underground trend, have become widespread, with many organized across the city since autumn 2023.
Bouldering rejects ropes and harnesses for typically shorter climbs, and its origins trace back to the alpine training regimens of mountaineers.
John Sherman popularized the V-scale for grading boulder problems; the bouldering boom came in the late 20th century.
The annual Boulder Bash last occurred on September 15, 2023, celebrating bouldering subculture.
Emma Davidson and Luke Martinez began as neophytes on local walls and now mentor the next generation of climbers.
